intended_object: The canonical Lie algebra isomorphism Lie(GLₙ)_B ≅ 𝔤𝔩ₙ(B). It sends a tangent vector at the identity, given as an R-derivation of the coordinate Hopf algebra O(GLₙ) with values in B via the counit, to the matrix of its values on the coordinate functions X_ij. The convolution bracket goes to the matrix commutator. This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Milne, *Algebraic Groups* §10.
explanation:
The forward map is `tangentMatrix`, which sends a derivation d to the matrix (d(X_ij)) after the coefficient identification `algEquivSelf`. The inverse comes from `tangentLinearEquivMatrix`, which is built with `LinearEquiv.ofBijective`. Injectivity and surjectivity are proved through dual-number points: the matrices that reduce to the identity are exactly those of the form 1 + εX.

The bracket condition is `tangentMatrix_lie`. It holds because Δ(X_ij) = Σ_k X_ik ⊗ X_kj, so (d⋆e)(X_ij) = (DE)_ij, and the convolution commutator therefore becomes the matrix commutator DE − ED. This is the standard convention for Lie(GLₙ).

The construction is general: any commutative base ring R and any commutative R-algebra B of coefficients. Indexing by `Fin n` matches the library's definition of GLₙ through `coordinateHopfAlgebra n`, and it is the standard way of writing GLₙ. Mathlib has no Hopf-algebra model of GLₙ and no Lie-algebra comparison of this kind, so there is no broader counterpart. Since the map is a bundled equivalence whose properties are all proved, it matches the intended canonical isomorphism.
